sources.why: OutdoorGearLab tests 200W panels only, no stations or kits, no sub-$250 picks
affiliate under-$500 station roundup with scores but no testing; stations only, no panel kits
single Explorer 300 Plus review by 'Editorial Team' citing deal sites; station only, no kit
camping power station roundup, no evident testing, no bundled panel pricing under $250
affiliate gift guide, but names a specific kit under $250 (ALLPOWERS VOLIX P300 256Wh + 100W panel, $208.99)
Outdoor Life tested solar generators but all picks are $1,000+ class, nothing near $250
Jackery-only model chooser, steers to $559 unit; off-budget
useful station/panel/cable matching logic but every kit is $450+
measured capacity with energy clamp and solar charge times on a 100W panel; notes EcoFlow River 3 ~$249 bundled with panel and a $120 budget unit

missing: A tested head-to-head of complete station+panel bundles that actually land under $250 (e.g., ALLPOWERS VOLIX P300 kit, EcoFlow River 3 + 45W bundle, Anker C300 DC with a cheap panel), with measured real-world solar recharge time from the bundled panel, usable Wh, and current street prices—no source compares kits at this budget.
why: The two major reviewers (OutdoorGearLab, Outdoor Life) cover panels alone or $1,000+ generators and never touch a $250 kit. Only solarscout [9], a small site with its own measurements, gets close by mentioning a ~$249 River 3 bundle, and the one source naming a sub-$250 kit outright [5] is an affiliate gift listicle. One substantive niche reviewer partially answering, no major-reviewer coverage, makes this contested rather than saturated or open.
